acceptance: Link targets with raw, entity-encoded or percent-encoded control characters, `javascript:` behind an entity colon, `vbscript:` and `data:` schemes, scheme-relative URLs and credentials never open; https, relative paths and fragments open, a URL in its canonical form. An inline `<a>` whose href the policy refuses stays visible source, and a safe one is followed only through the policy to its canonical URL.

reason: TS builds a serializable Markdown link index in a Web Worker (one document read at a time, superseded builds cancelled, saved documents re-indexed) holding path resolution and backlinks with bounded excerpts and snapshot sizes. Backlinks have no product surface, and native link resolution reads the Explorer's file metadata when a link is decorated or followed, so there is no index, worker or backlink snapshot.

acceptance: A link navigates only to an executable target: a heading of this document, a workspace file or a safe external URL (canonical), never while its source is being edited; a missing heading or wiki target, an unsafe href, or a workspace link without a workspace leads nowhere. Heading fragments cover ATX, setext, Unicode and numbered duplicates and stay exact across incremental edits. A link opens on a stationary click that keeps the selection; leaving the drag threshold cancels it.

reason: A browser fires a click after the pointer release TS already handled, so TS must swallow exactly that paired click. GPUI delivers one mouse-up and no synthetic click after it, so there is nothing to suppress.

acceptance: In a focused Markdown editor ⌘B, ⌘I, ⌘U, ⌘D and ⌘⇧X format the selection (strong, emphasis, underline, strike); ⌘⇧B, Option or Control chords on macOS do not, and an editor without focus is never formatted.

reason: GPUI dispatches a held keystroke to its action again on every key repeat, so holding ⌘B toggles bold on and off natively; the product ignores auto-repeated format shortcuts (and Option, Control-on-macOS and released inputs, which the native key bindings also ignore).

Electron's main process sees keys before the renderer, so TS tracks which window has a focused Markdown editor over trusted IPC and forwards format shortcuts to it. The native editor binds its shortcuts in its own key context, which is active only while it has focus.
